# Collaborative Effort Delivers $13 Million in Critical Medical Aid to Sudan Amid Ongoing Violence

![Image 3](https://www.projecthope.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/0004_SDN_MedicalDelivery_10_2023-1-aspect-ratio-1200-675.webp)

Washington, DC – In response to the escalating violence in Sudan, [Project HOPE](https://www.projecthope.org/), [Airlink](https://airlinkflight.org/) and key partners, including [MAP International](https://www.map.org/), [Flexport.org](https://www.flexport.org/), [Astral Aviation](https://astral-aviation.com/), and [Qatar Airways](https://www.qatarairways.com/en-us/homepage.html), have successfully coordinated the delivery of $13 million (24,000 pounds) worth of vital medical supplies, pharmaceuticals, hygiene supplies, and therapeutic food to Sudan. [The Sudanese American Physicians Association (SAPA)](https://sapa-usa.org/) and Project HOPE will oversee the distribution of the shipment, ensuring that hospitals and health facilities facing the most critical shortages receive the supplies necessary to continue their vital work in treating patients.

The shipment includes essential medical supplies, ranging from syringes, gauze, and wound care items to medications, including antibiotics, antiparasitics, and pain relievers. Additionally, it includes prenatal vitamins, oral rehydration tablets, hygiene supplies, and protective equipment. Recognizing the exacerbated food insecurity across the entire Horn of Africa due to prolonged drought, the shipment also incorporates therapeutic food. The shipment will support over 100,000 people across Sudan where communities are grappling with under-resourced health facilities and cholera and dengue outbreaks.

“This shipment is a lifeline for many hospitals that are lacking the supplies and resources to address the influx of patients seeking care and lifesaving medication for everything from cholera to gunshot wounds to pregnancy,” said Arlan Fuller, Director of Emergency Preparedness and Response for Project HOPE. “This partnership exemplifies the essence of humanitarianism — nonprofits and corporations coming together to share resources and knowledge to reach those who need support the most.”

“Airlink’s partners have struggled to get needed medical aid into Sudan since the conflict broke out in April, owing to the limited flight options and high cost of airlift into Port Sudan – the country’s only operating airport. We are proud to say, we’ve found a way to get aid there,” said Steve Smith, Airlink President & CEO. “By bringing together our donors and partners in the private sector – Astral Aviation, Flexport.org, and Qatar Airways Cargo – and coordinating this shipment with long-time nonprofit partner Project HOPE, we’ve been able to make the impossible possible in the midst of one of the most challenging humanitarian crises facing the world. We hope this is just the start of our work in Sudan, breaking down the logistical barriers to get aid where it is needed most.”

“MAP International’s participation in this collaborative effort to deliver $13 million in critical medical aid to Sudan underscores our commitment to making a meaningful impact on global health crises. In timesof escalating violence and dire need, it is imperative that organizations and partners unite to provide essential medical supplies, pharmaceuticals, and support to vulnerable communitie,” said Steve Stirling, President and CEO, MAP International. “Together with our dedicated partners, we are honored to be a part of this vital mission, which will help save lives and alleviate suffering in Sudan and the Horn of Africa.”

“SAPA is honored to continue supporting health personnel in Sudan who have been working tirelessly to provide essential medical services. This shipment will ensure that hospitals and doctors on the ground are able to obtain the supplies necessary to carry out their incredible work,” said Dr. Yasir Elamin, President of SAPA. “We are grateful for the opportunity to collaborate with Project HOPE and so many incredible partners to deliver much-needed medical aid to the region.”

“Flexport.org is thankful for our strong partnerships that enable the effective and efficient delivery of lifesaving humanitarian aid, and to our donors like Tech For Refugees, a non-profit that supports refugee relief efforts through technology,” Kristen Czapar Dohnt, Head of Flexport.org.

“Astral Aviation is proud of its association with Airlink and to be of service to its partners by providing a dedicated charter from its Nairobi Hub to Port Sudan on the Boeing 727F with 10782 kgs of humanitarian cargoes,” said Mike Mutahi, Chief Operating Officer of Astral Aviation. “Astral Aviation will continue to cooperate with our partners in delivering humanitarian cargoes to regions in Africa and Middle East with its dedicated fleet and expertise.”

Photos are available [here](https://projecthope.canto.com/s/N2OSO?viewIndex=1). To schedule an interview, please contact [media@projecthope.org](mailto:media@projecthope.org).

###

**About Project HOPE**  
Founded in 1958, Project HOPE is a leading global health and humanitarian organization operating in more than 20 countries around the world. We respond to emergencies and work side-by-side with local health systems to improve health outcomes. For more information on Project HOPE and its work around the world, visit www.ProjectHOPE.org and follow us on Twitter and Instagram @ProjectHOPEorg.

**About Airlink**  
Airlink is a nonprofit organization providing free air transport and logistical coordination for pre-screened nonprofits to deliver disaster responders and supplies in the wake of humanitarian crises worldwide. Its network includes over 200 aid organizations and 50 air carriers and logistics partners. Its first mission was in response to the Haiti earthquake. Since its inception in 2010, Airlink’s airline partners have flown more than 11,000 relief workers and transported 12 million pounds of humanitarian cargo, saving nonprofits over $33 million in air transport costs, directly helping over 46 million people. In addition, Airlink receives in-kind gifts from airlines and donations from organizations and individuals within the aviation sector. For more information, visit www.airlinkflight.org.

**About MAP International**  
MAP International is a non-profit global health organization dedicated to providing medicine for all people. With a strong focus on delivering medical aid in times of crisis, MAP International works collaboratively with partners and donors to improve the health and well-being of communities facing significant challenges. Through our mission-driven approach, we strive to make a positive impact on the lives of those in need, particularly in regions experiencing conflict and humanitarian emergencies. Learn more about our work at www.map.org.

**About Flexport.org**Flexport.org is the dedicated sustainability and impact team within Flexport that enables organizations to deliver aid and meet their decarbonization goals with greater ease and lower costs. Flexport.org creates value-added services for Flexport users to measure and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, bringing sustainability into the forefront of their business roadmap. Flexport.org also provides critically needed visibility and expertise to nonprofits and NGOs, governments, and social enterprises, helping deliver humanitarian aid, disaster relief and development shipments where they are needed most. To date, we have delivered over 74 million pounds of aid in 3,984 shipments, impacting 120 million people globally. For more information, visit www.flexport.org.

**About Astral Aviation**Astral Aviation is a dedicated cargo airline which is based at the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi, Kenya, and operates a fleet of 15 cargo aircrafts to over 50 destinations in Africa, from its hubs in Nairobi, Johannesburg, Liege, Dubai and Hong Kong. Celebrating its 23rd Anniversary in 2023, Astral is the fastest growing Cargo Airline in Africa with a diversified fleet capacity which ranges from 5 tons to 110 tons and has recently taken delivery of its Boeing 757-200 Freighter. The following events occurred in **March 1942**:

## [March 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1 "March 1"), 1942 (Sunday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: March 1, 1942 (Sunday)")]

*   The [Second Battle of the Java Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_the_Java_Sea "Second Battle of the Java Sea") was fought, resulting in Japanese victory. The cruiser [HMS _Exeter_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Exeter_(68) "HMS Exeter (68)") and the destroyers [HMS _Encounter_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Encounter_(H10) "HMS Encounter (H10)") and [USS _Pope_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Pope_(DD-225) "USS Pope (DD-225)") were sunk.
*   The [Battle of Sunda Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Sunda_Strait "Battle of Sunda Strait") ended in Japanese victory. The Allies lost 1 heavy cruiser, 1 light cruiser and 1 destroyer while the Japanese lost 1 minelayer and 4 troopships sunk or grounded.
*   Construction of the [Sobibór extermination camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobib%C3%B3r_extermination_camp "Sobibór extermination camp") began.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-1)
*   Near [Christmas Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Island "Christmas Island"), the fuel tanker [USS _Pecos_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Pecos_(AO-6) "USS Pecos (AO-6)") was bombed and sunk by [Aichi D3A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aichi_D3A "Aichi D3A") dive bombers, while the American destroyer [USS _Edsall_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Edsall_(DD-219) "USS Edsall (DD-219)") was bombed and damaged by Japanese aircraft and then shelled and sunk by the battleships _[Hiei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_battleship\_Hiei "Japanese battleship Hiei")_ and _[Kirishima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_battleship\_Kirishima "Japanese battleship Kirishima")_.
*   The Dutch steamship _[Roseboom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS\_Rooseboom "SS Rooseboom")_ was torpedoed and sunk west of Sumatra by the Japanese submarine _[I-159](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_submarine\_I-159 "Japanese submarine I-159")_.
*   German submarine _[U-656](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-656 "German submarine U-656")_ was depth charged and sunk off [Cape Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Race "Cape Race"), [Newfoundland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland_(island) "Newfoundland (island)") by an American [Lockheed Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Hudson "Lockheed Hudson").

## [March 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_3 "March 3"), 1942 (Tuesday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: March 3, 1942 (Tuesday)")]

*   The [Battle of Pegu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Pegu "Battle of Pegu"), concerning the defence of [Rangoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangon "Yangon"), began.
*   [Attack on Broome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Broome "Attack on Broome"): Japanese fighter planes attacked the town of [Broome, Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broome,_Western_Australia "Broome, Western Australia") and killed 88 people.
*   [KNILM Douglas DC-3 shootdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942_KNILM_Douglas_DC-3_shootdown "1942 KNILM Douglas DC-3 shootdown"): A [Douglas DC-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_DC-3 "Douglas DC-3") airliner was shot down over Australia by Japanese warplanes, resulting in the deaths of four passengers and the loss of diamonds worth an estimated [A£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_pound "Australian pound") 150,000–300,000. The diamonds were presumably looted from the crash site but their fate remains a mystery.
*   The American gunboat _[Asheville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS\_Asheville\_(PG-21) "USS Asheville (PG-21)")_ was sunk south of Java by the Japanese destroyers _[Arashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_destroyer\_Arashi "Japanese destroyer Arashi")_ and _[Nowaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_destroyer\_Nowaki\_(1940) "Japanese destroyer Nowaki (1940)")_.
*   An exhibition titled "Artists in Exile" opened at the [Pierre Matisse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Matisse "Pierre Matisse") Gallery in New York. Fourteen artists including [Marc Chagall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Chagall "Marc Chagall"), [Max Ernst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Ernst "Max Ernst"), [Fernand Léger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernand_L%C3%A9ger "Fernand Léger") and [Piet Mondrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piet_Mondrian "Piet Mondrian") were represented at the exhibition with one piece each.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-6)
*   German submarine _[U-92](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-92\_(1942) "German submarine U-92 (1942)")_ was commissioned.
*   **Died:**[Prince Amedeo, Duke of Aosta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Amedeo,_Duke_of_Aosta "Prince Amedeo, Duke of Aosta"), 43, Italian prince (died in a POW camp in Nairobi)

## [March 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_4 "March 4"), 1942 (Wednesday)

    *   [Jerry Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Sloan "Jerry Sloan"), basketball player and coach, in [McLeansboro, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLeansboro,_Illinois "McLeansboro, Illinois") (d. 2020)

*   **Died:**[Pompiliu Ștefu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompiliu_%C8%98tefu "Pompiliu Ștefu"), 31, Romanian typographer, communist activist and anti-fascist militant (executed)

## [March 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_29 "March 29"), 1942 (Sunday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: March 29, 1942 (Sunday)")]

*   The [Battle of Toungoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Toungoo "Battle of Toungoo") ended in Japanese victory.
*   [Stafford Cripps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stafford_Cripps "Stafford Cripps") met with [Mahatma Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi") in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi") and presented his plan for postwar independence for India.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-chronicle_of_the_20th_c.-27)
*   The British cargo ship _[Hertford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertford\_(1920) "Hertford (1920)")_ was torpedoed and sunk south of [Halifax, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax,_Nova_Scotia "Halifax, Nova Scotia") by German submarine _[U-571](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-571 "German submarine U-571")_.
*   German destroyer _[Z26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_destroyer\_Z26 "German destroyer Z26")_ was shelled and sunk in the Barents Sea by British cruiser _[Trinidad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_Trinidad\_(46) "HMS Trinidad (46)")_ and destroyer _[Eclipse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_Eclipse\_(H08) "HMS Eclipse (H08)")_.
*   The [Hukbalahap Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hukbalahap_Rebellion "Hukbalahap Rebellion") began when former [Hukbalahap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hukbalahap "Hukbalahap") soldiers rebelled against the Philippine government. The rebellion would not end until 1954.
*   Following a coup d'état, the Free Republic of Nias was proclaimed by a group of freed Nazi German prisoners in the Indonesian island of [Nias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nias "Nias"). The republic existed for less than a month until the island was fully occupied by Japanese troops.
*   **Born:**
    *   [Kenichi Ogata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenichi_Ogata_(voice_actor) "Kenichi Ogata (voice actor)"), voice actor, in [Tagawa District, Fukuoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagawa_District,_Fukuoka "Tagawa District, Fukuoka"), [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan");
    *   [Scott Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Wilson_(actor) "Scott Wilson (actor)"), actor, in [Thomasville, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomasville,_Georgia "Thomasville, Georgia") (d. 2018)

*   **Died:**[Yogbir Singh Kansakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yogbir_Singh_Kansakar "Yogbir Singh Kansakar"), 56, Nepalese poet and social reformer

## [March 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_30 "March 30"), 1942 (Monday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: March 30, 1942 (Monday)")]

*   As a result of the collapse of [American-British-Dutch-Australian Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American-British-Dutch-Australian_Command "American-British-Dutch-Australian Command") (ABDACOM), the US [Joint Chiefs of Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff "Joint Chiefs of Staff") assumed responsibility for control of Allied forces in the Pacific; these were divided into several supreme commands, including [Pacific Ocean Areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean_Areas_(command) "Pacific Ocean Areas (command)") (POA), under Admiral [Chester Nimitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_Nimitz "Chester Nimitz") and [South West Pacific Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Pacific_Area_(command) "South West Pacific Area (command)") (SWPA), under General [Douglas MacArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_MacArthur "Douglas MacArthur").
*   German submarine _[U-585](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-585 "German submarine U-585")_ struck a naval mine and sank in the Barents Sea.
*   The exclusion of [Japanese-American internees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internment_of_Japanese_Americans "Internment of Japanese Americans") began in [Bainbridge Island, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bainbridge_Island,_Washington "Bainbridge Island, Washington").
*   **Born:**[Ruben Kun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruben_Kun "Ruben Kun"), [President of Nauru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Nauru "President of Nauru"), in [Nauru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nauru "Nauru") (d. 2014)

## [March 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_31 "March 31"), 1942 (Tuesday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: March 31, 1942 (Tuesday)")]

*   The Japanese began the [Indian Ocean raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_raid "Indian Ocean raid").
*   The [Battle of Christmas Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Christmas_Island "Battle of Christmas Island") was fought. Japanese soldiers were able to occupy [Christmas Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Island "Christmas Island") without resistance, although the American submarine _[Seawolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS\_Seawolf\_(SS-197) "USS Seawolf (SS-197)")_ damaged the Japanese cruiser _[Naka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_cruiser\_Naka "Japanese cruiser Naka")_.
*   Allied convoy [PQ 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_13 "Convoy PQ 13") reached [Murmansk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murmansk "Murmansk") despite fierce German attacks.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-chronicle_of_the_20th_c.-27)
*   German submarine _[U-353](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-353 "German submarine U-353")_ was commissioned.

The following events occurred in **March 1942**:

## [March 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1 "March 1"), 1942 (Sunday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: March 1, 1942 (Sunday)")]

*   The [Second Battle of the Java Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_the_Java_Sea "Second Battle of the Java Sea") was fought, resulting in Japanese victory. The cruiser [HMS _Exeter_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Exeter_(68) "HMS Exeter (68)") and the destroyers [HMS _Encounter_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Encounter_(H10) "HMS Encounter (H10)") and [USS _Pope_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Pope_(DD-225) "USS Pope (DD-225)") were sunk.
*   The [Battle of Sunda Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Sunda_Strait "Battle of Sunda Strait") ended in Japanese victory. The Allies lost 1 heavy cruiser, 1 light cruiser and 1 destroyer while the Japanese lost 1 minelayer and 4 troopships sunk or grounded.
*   Construction of the [Sobibór extermination camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobib%C3%B3r_extermination_camp "Sobibór extermination camp") began.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-1)
*   Near [Christmas Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Island "Christmas Island"), the fuel tanker [USS _Pecos_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Pecos_(AO-6) "USS Pecos (AO-6)") was bombed and sunk by [Aichi D3A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aichi_D3A "Aichi D3A") dive bombers, while the American destroyer [USS _Edsall_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Edsall_(DD-219) "USS Edsall (DD-219)") was bombed and damaged by Japanese aircraft and then shelled and sunk by the battleships _[Hiei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_battleship\_Hiei "Japanese battleship Hiei")_ and _[Kirishima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_battleship\_Kirishima "Japanese battleship Kirishima")_.
*   The Dutch steamship _[Roseboom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS\_Rooseboom "SS Rooseboom")_ was torpedoed and sunk west of Sumatra by the Japanese submarine _[I-159](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_submarine\_I-159 "Japanese submarine I-159")_.
*   German submarine _[U-656](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-656 "German submarine U-656")_ was depth charged and sunk off [Cape Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Race "Cape Race"), [Newfoundland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland_(island) "Newfoundland (island)") by an American [Lockheed Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Hudson "Lockheed Hudson").
*   **Died:**[George S. Rentz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_S._Rentz "George S. Rentz"), 59, [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") chaplain (killed in action); [Cornelius Vanderbilt III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornelius_Vanderbilt_III "Cornelius Vanderbilt III"), 68, American military officer, inventor, engineer and yachtsman

## [March 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_2 "March 2"), 1942 (Monday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: March 2, 1942 (Monday)")]

*   The Japanese began heavy air strikes on [New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Guinea "New Guinea") in preparation for an invasion.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-williams-2)
*   [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia") declared war on [Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand "Thailand").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-doody-3)
*   Ships at [Surabaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surabaya "Surabaya") in the Dutch East Indies were scuttled to keep them from being captured by the Japanese.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-5)
*   The American destroyer _[Pillsbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS\_Pillsbury\_(DD-227) "USS Pillsbury (DD-227)")_ was shelled and sunk west of [Christmas Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Island "Christmas Island") by the Japanese cruisers _[Atago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_cruiser\_Atago "Japanese cruiser Atago")_ and _[Takao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_cruiser\_Takao\_(1930) "Japanese cruiser Takao (1930)")_.
*   **Born:**
    *   [John Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Irving "John Irving"), novelist and screenwriter, in [Exeter, New Hampshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exeter,_New_Hampshire "Exeter, New Hampshire");
    *   [Claude Larose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Larose_(ice_hockey,_born_1942) "Claude Larose (ice hockey, born 1942)"), ice hockey player, in [Hearst, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearst,_Ontario "Hearst, Ontario"), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada");
    *   [Lou Reed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Reed "Lou Reed"), musician, in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)") (d. 2013)

*   The [Battle of Yunnan-Burma Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Yunnan-Burma_Road "Battle of Yunnan-Burma Road") had its first clash when the two-day [Battle of Tachiao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Tachiao "Battle of Tachiao") began.
*   President Roosevelt signed [Executive Order 9102](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Order_9102 "Executive Order 9102"), ordering the creation of the [War Relocation Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_Relocation_Authority "War Relocation Authority").
*   German submarine _[U-411](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-411 "German submarine U-411")_ was commissioned.
*   The [Cecil B. DeMille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cecil_B._DeMille "Cecil B. DeMille")-directed adventure film _[Reap the Wild Wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reap\_the\_Wild\_Wind "Reap the Wild Wind")_ starring [Ray Milland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Milland "Ray Milland") and [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne") was released.

## [March 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_19 "March 19"), 1942 (Thursday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: March 19, 1942 (Thursday)")]

*   The [Battle of Tachiao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Tachiao "Battle of Tachiao") ended when the Japanese captured [Pyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyu "Pyu").
*   The [Battle of Toungoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Toungoo "Battle of Toungoo") began.
*   The American tanker _[Papoose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS\_Papoose "SS Papoose")_ was torpedoed and sunk 15 nautical miles southeast of [Cape Lookout, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Lookout_(North_Carolina) "Cape Lookout (North Carolina)") by German submarine _[U-124](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-124\_(1940) "German submarine U-124 (1940)")_.
*   German submarine _[U-614](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-614 "German submarine U-614")_ was commissioned.
*   **Died:**[José Díaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_D%C3%ADaz_(Spanish_politician) "José Díaz (Spanish politician)"), 46, Spanish communist politician (died in [Tbilisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tbilisi "Tbilisi"), [Georgian SSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic") of apparent suicide)

## [March 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_20 "March 20"), 1942 (Friday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: March 20, 1942 (Friday)")]

*   The [Battle of Oktwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Oktwin "Battle of Oktwin") in the Burma Campaign began.
*   When reporters met the train of General [Douglas MacArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_MacArthur "Douglas MacArthur") north of [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide"), Australia, he declared: "The President of the United States ordered me to break through the Japanese lines and proceed from Corregidor to Australia for the purpose, as I understand it, of organizing the American offensive against Japan, a primary object of which is the relief of the Philippines. I came through and I shall return."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-28)
*   The British destroyer _Heythrop_ was torpedoed northeast of [Bardia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bardia "Bardia") by German submarine _[U-652](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-652 "German submarine U-652")_. She was towed by the destroyer _[Eridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_Eridge\_(L68) "HMS Eridge (L68)")_ towards [Tobruk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobruk "Tobruk") but foundered five hours later.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-29)

## [March 21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_21 "March 21"), 1942 (Saturday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: March 21, 1942 (Saturday)")]

*   The last British cavalry charge in history occurred when about 60 Sikh sowars of the [Burma Frontier Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burma_Frontier_Force "Burma Frontier Force") attacked Japanese infantry at [Taungoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taungoo "Taungoo"). Most were killed.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-31)
*   German submarines _[U-442](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-442 "German submarine U-442")_ and _[U-517](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-517 "German submarine U-517")_ were commissioned.
*   The spy film _[Secret Agent of Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret\_Agent\_of\_Japan "Secret Agent of Japan")_ starring [Preston Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_Foster "Preston Foster") premiered at the Globe Theatre in New York City. It was the first film to include the [attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor") as part of the plot.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-32)
*   **Born:**[Ali Abdullah Saleh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Abdullah_Saleh "Ali Abdullah Saleh"), 1st President of Yemen, in [Al-Ahmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashid "Hashid"), [Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemen "Yemen") (d. 2017)
*   **Died:**
    *   [J. S. Woodsworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._S._Woodsworth "J. S. Woodsworth"), 67, Canadian politician;
    *   [Václav Morávek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%A1clav_Mor%C3%A1vek "Václav Morávek"), 37, Czechoslovak Brigadier General and national hero (killed in a gunfight with the [Gestapo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gestapo "Gestapo"))

## [March 22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_22 "March 22"), 1942 (Sunday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: March 22, 1942 (Sunday)")]

*   [Second Battle of Sirte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_Sirte "Second Battle of Sirte"), the escorting warships of a British convoy to Malta held off a much more powerful Regia Marina (Italian Navy) squadron.
*   Allied forces abandoned the Magwe airfield in [Burma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myanmar "Myanmar"), 100 miles (160 km) east of [Akyab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sittwe "Sittwe").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-ww2_timelines_mar_22-33)
*   [Cripps' mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cripps'_mission "Cripps' mission"): The British government sent [Stafford Cripps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stafford_Cripps "Stafford Cripps") to India to disclose the British constitutional proposals for a postwar India. Britain promised self-government for India after the war in exchange for their co-operation in the war effort.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-ww2_timelines_mar_22-33)
*   The [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") began transmitting news bulletins in [Morse Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morse_Code "Morse Code") for the benefit of resistance fighters in occupied Europe.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-34)
*   The [Manzanar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manzanar "Manzanar") Japanese-American internment camp first opened.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-35)

## [March 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_23 "March 23"), 1942 (Monday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: March 23, 1942 (Monday)")]

*   The [Japanese occupation of the Andaman Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_occupation_of_the_Andaman_Islands "Japanese occupation of the Andaman Islands") began.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-36)
*   The British tanker _[British Prudence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV\_British\_Prudence "MV British Prudence")_ was torpedoed and sunk in the Atlantic Ocean by the German submarine _[U-754](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-754 "German submarine U-754")_.
*   Hitler issued [Directive No. 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Adolf_Hitler's_directives "List of Adolf Hitler's directives"), pertaining to the command organization of the [Atlantic Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Wall "Atlantic Wall").
*   German submarine _[U-166](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-166\_(1941) "German submarine U-166 (1941)")_ was commissioned.
*   **Born:**[Walter Rodney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Rodney "Walter Rodney"), historian, political activist and scholar, in [British Guiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Guiana "British Guiana") (d. 1980)
*   **Died:**
    *   [Marcelo Torcuato de Alvear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelo_Torcuato_de_Alvear "Marcelo Torcuato de Alvear"), 73, 20th [President of Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Argentina "President of Argentina")
    *   [Franz Walter Stahlecker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Walter_Stahlecker "Franz Walter Stahlecker"), 41, commander of [Einsatzgruppe A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Einsatzgruppe_A "Einsatzgruppe A"), killed by [Soviet partisans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_partisans "Soviet partisans")

## [March 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_24 "March 24"), 1942 (Tuesday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: March 24, 1942 (Tuesday)")]

*   The [Battle of Oktwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Oktwin "Battle of Oktwin") ended when the Chinese fell back to the main defensive line at Toungoo.
*   The British destroyer _[Southwold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_Southwold\_(L10) "HMS Southwold (L10)")_ sank off Malta after hitting a naval mine.
*   German submarine _[U-655](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-655 "German submarine U-655")_ was rammed and sunk in the [Barents Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barents_Sea "Barents Sea") by the minesweeper HMS _Sharpshooter_.
*   The romantic drama film _[To the Shores of Tripoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_the\_Shores\_of\_Tripoli "To the Shores of Tripoli")_ starring [John Payne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Payne_(actor) "John Payne (actor)"), [Maureen O'Hara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maureen_O'Hara "Maureen O'Hara") and [Randolph Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph_Scott "Randolph Scott") had its world premiere in [San Diego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California").

## [March 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_25 "March 25"), 1942 (Wednesday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: March 25, 1942 (Wednesday)")]

*   British destroyer _[Jaguar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_Jaguar\_(F34) "HMS Jaguar (F34)")_ was torpedoed and sunk in the Mediterranean Sea off [Sidi Barrani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidi_Barrani "Sidi Barrani") by German submarine _[U-652](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-652 "German submarine U-652")_.
*   British destroyer _[Legion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_Legion\_(G74) "HMS Legion (G74)")_ and submarine _[P39](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_P39 "HMS P39")_ were bombed and sunk in the [Grand Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Harbor "Grand Harbor"), [Valletta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valletta "Valletta"), Malta.
*   The [White House Communications Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Communications_Agency "White House Communications Agency") was formed.
*   [Holocaust in Slovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust_in_Slovakia "Holocaust in Slovakia"): The [first mass transport of Jews to Auschwitz concentration camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_mass_transport_of_Jews_to_Auschwitz_concentration_camp "First mass transport of Jews to Auschwitz concentration camp") departed from [Poprad railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poprad-Tatry_railway_station "Poprad-Tatry railway station") in the [Slovak Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovak_Republic_(1939%E2%80%931945) "Slovak Republic (1939–1945)"), consisting of 997 young women.
*   **Born:**[Aretha Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aretha_Franklin "Aretha Franklin"), soul singer, in [Memphis, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee") (d. 2018)

## [March 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_26 "March 26"), 1942 (Thursday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: March 26, 1942 (Thursday)")]

*   The [Battle of Suursaari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Suursaari "Battle of Suursaari") began on the frozen [Gulf of Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Finland "Gulf of Finland") between Finnish and Soviet forces.
*   The Second [Dünamünde Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C3%BCnam%C3%BCnde_Action "Dünamünde Action") massacred another 1,840 people near [Riga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riga "Riga").
*   The Nazis began the deportation of Jews to [Auschwitz concentration camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz_concentration_camp "Auschwitz concentration camp") with the transport of 1,000 single women from Slovakia via [Poprad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poprad "Poprad") transit camp.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-chronicle_of_the_20th_c.-27) This was also the first deportation of Slovak Jews; of the 57,000 deported in 1942 only a few hundred survived the Holocaust.
*   The Germans launched [Operation Bamberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Bamberg "Operation Bamberg"), an anti-partisan operation in occupied Belarus.
*   Police in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro") announced that they had smashed a [Nazi spy ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Bol%C3%ADvar "Operation Bolívar") with the arrest of 200 operatives.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-37)
*   The ruling [Wafd Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wafd_Party "Wafd Party") won [parliamentary elections in Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_parliamentary_election,_1942 "Egyptian parliamentary election, 1942").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-chronology_and_index-38)
*   German submarines _[U-337](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-337 "German submarine U-337")_ and _[U-615](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-615 "German submarine U-615")_ was commissioned.
*   The [USS _Atik_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Atik "USS Atik") was torpedoed and sunk in action by _U-123_, all hands on board the Q-ship were lost.
*   The tanker [SS _Dixie Arrow_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Dixie_Arrow "SS Dixie Arrow") was torpedoed off [Cape Hatteras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Hatteras "Cape Hatteras") by _U-71_
*   **Born:**[Erica Jong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erica_Jong "Erica Jong"), author and teacher, in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City")

## [March 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_27 "March 27"), 1942 (Friday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: March 27, 1942 (Friday)")]

*   For French Jews, deportations began when the first convoy left Paris for [Auschwitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitz "Auschwitz").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-39)
*   The Australian government imposed a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") over the northern portion of the continent.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-40)
*   The [Action of 27 March 1942](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_of_27_March_1942 "Action of 27 March 1942") was fought in the Atlantic Ocean. German submarine _[U-123](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-123\_(1940) "German submarine U-123 (1940)")_ sank the American [Q-ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q-ship "Q-ship")[USS _Atik_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Atik_(AK-101) "USS Atik (AK-101)").
*   German submarine _[U-587](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-587 "German submarine U-587")_ was depth charged and sunk in the Atlantic Ocean by British warships.
*   [Joe Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Louis "Joe Louis") knocked out [Abe Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abe_Simon "Abe Simon") in the sixth round at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden_(1925) "Madison Square Garden (1925)") to retain the World Heavyweight Boxing Championship.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-41)
*   The [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy") merchant steamship [_Oreste_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Oreste?action=edit&redlink=1 "SS Oreste (page does not exist)"), sailing from [Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split,_Croatia "Split, Croatia") to [Bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro"), struck a [mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_mine "Naval mine") around 10:00 local time near [Jaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaz_Beach "Jaz Beach") and sank.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-42)
*   **Born:**
    *   [John Sulston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sulston "John Sulston"), biologist, in [Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge "Cambridge"), England (d. 2018);
    *   [Michael York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_York "Michael York"), actor, in [Fulmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulmer "Fulmer"), [Buckinghamshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckinghamshire "Buckinghamshire"), England

*   **Died:**
    *   [Julio González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Gonz%C3%A1lez_(sculptor) "Julio González (sculptor)"), 65, Spanish sculptor;
    *   [John W. Wilcox, Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_W._Wilcox,_Jr. "John W. Wilcox, Jr."), 60, American admiral (lost overboard in stormy weather)

## [March 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_28 "March 28"), 1942 (Saturday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: March 28, 1942 (Saturday)")]

*   The Japanese completed the [invasion of Sumatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Sumatra_(1942) "Invasion of Sumatra (1942)").
*   [Bombing of Lübeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombing_of_L%C3%BCbeck_in_World_War_II "Bombing of Lübeck in World War II"): The port city of [Lübeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%BCbeck "Lübeck") was the first German city attacked in substantial numbers by the [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force"). The night attack caused a [firestorm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firestorm "Firestorm") that caused severe damage to the historic centre and led to the retaliatory [Baedeker raids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baedeker_Blitz "Baedeker Blitz") on historic British cities.
*   The British conducted the [St Nazaire Raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Nazaire_Raid "St Nazaire Raid") on the heavily defended [Normandie dry dock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Joubert_Lock "Louis Joubert Lock") at [Saint-Nazaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Nazaire "Saint-Nazaire") in German-occupied France. All British objectives were achieved although 169 were killed and 215 taken prisoner. The destroyer [HMS _Campelltown_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Campbeltown_(I42) "HMS Campbeltown (I42)") was expended as a floating bomb.
*   The Panamanian cargo ship _[Howick Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS\_Howick\_Hall\_(ID-1303) "USS Howick Hall (ID-1303)")_ of convoy [PQ 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_13 "Convoy PQ 13") was bombed and sunk in the Barents Sea by [Junkers Ju 88](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junkers_Ju_88 "Junkers Ju 88") aircraft.
*   German submarine _[U-261](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-261 "German submarine U-261")_ was commissioned.
*   [Stanford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1941%E2%80%9342_Stanford_Indians_men's_basketball_team "1941–42 Stanford Indians men's basketball team") beat [Dartmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartmouth_Big_Green_men's_basketball "Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball") 53–38 in the [NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Tournament "1942 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament") Final.
*   **Born:**
    *   [Daniel Dennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Dennett "Daniel Dennett"), philosopher, writer and cognitive scientist, in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts"); (d. 2024)
    *   [Neil Kinnock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Kinnock "Neil Kinnock"), politician, in [Tredegar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tredegar "Tredegar"), [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales "Wales");
    *   [Mike Newell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Newell_(director) "Mike Newell (director)"), film director and producer, in [St Albans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Albans "St Albans"), [Hertfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertfordshire "Hertfordshire"), England;
    *   [Conrad Schumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conrad_Schumann "Conrad Schumann"), East German border guard, in Zschochau, [Saxony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saxony "Saxony"), Germany (d. 1998);
    *   [Jerry Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Sloan "Jerry Sloan"), basketball player and coach, in [McLeansboro, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLeansboro,_Illinois "McLeansboro, Illinois") (d. 2020)

*   **Died:**[Pompiliu Ștefu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompiliu_%C8%98tefu "Pompiliu Ștefu"), 31, Romanian typographer, communist activist and anti-fascist militant (executed)

## [March 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_29 "March 29"), 1942 (Sunday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: March 29, 1942 (Sunday)")]

*   The [Battle of Toungoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Toungoo "Battle of Toungoo") ended in Japanese victory.
*   [Stafford Cripps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stafford_Cripps "Stafford Cripps") met with [Mahatma Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi") in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi") and presented his plan for postwar independence for India.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-chronicle_of_the_20th_c.-27)
*   The British cargo ship _[Hertford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertford\_(1920) "Hertford (1920)")_ was torpedoed and sunk south of [Halifax, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax,_Nova_Scotia "Halifax, Nova Scotia") by German submarine _[U-571](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-571 "German submarine U-571")_.
*   German destroyer _[Z26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_destroyer\_Z26 "German destroyer Z26")_ was shelled and sunk in the Barents Sea by British cruiser _[Trinidad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_Trinidad\_(46) "HMS Trinidad (46)")_ and destroyer _[Eclipse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS\_Eclipse\_(H08) "HMS Eclipse (H08)")_.
*   The [Hukbalahap Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hukbalahap_Rebellion "Hukbalahap Rebellion") began when former [Hukbalahap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hukbalahap "Hukbalahap") soldiers rebelled against the Philippine government. The rebellion would not end until 1954.
*   Following a coup d'état, the Free Republic of Nias was proclaimed by a group of freed Nazi German prisoners in the Indonesian island of [Nias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nias "Nias"). The republic existed for less than a month until the island was fully occupied by Japanese troops.
*   **Born:**
    *   [Kenichi Ogata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenichi_Ogata_(voice_actor) "Kenichi Ogata (voice actor)"), voice actor, in [Tagawa District, Fukuoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagawa_District,_Fukuoka "Tagawa District, Fukuoka"), [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan");
    *   [Scott Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Wilson_(actor) "Scott Wilson (actor)"), actor, in [Thomasville, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomasville,_Georgia "Thomasville, Georgia") (d. 2018)

*   **Died:**[Yogbir Singh Kansakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yogbir_Singh_Kansakar "Yogbir Singh Kansakar"), 56, Nepalese poet and social reformer

## [March 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_30 "March 30"), 1942 (Monday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: March 30, 1942 (Monday)")]

*   As a result of the collapse of [American-British-Dutch-Australian Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American-British-Dutch-Australian_Command "American-British-Dutch-Australian Command") (ABDACOM), the US [Joint Chiefs of Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff "Joint Chiefs of Staff") assumed responsibility for control of Allied forces in the Pacific; these were divided into several supreme commands, including [Pacific Ocean Areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean_Areas_(command) "Pacific Ocean Areas (command)") (POA), under Admiral [Chester Nimitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_Nimitz "Chester Nimitz") and [South West Pacific Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Pacific_Area_(command) "South West Pacific Area (command)") (SWPA), under General [Douglas MacArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_MacArthur "Douglas MacArthur").
*   German submarine _[U-585](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-585 "German submarine U-585")_ struck a naval mine and sank in the Barents Sea.
*   The exclusion of [Japanese-American internees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internment_of_Japanese_Americans "Internment of Japanese Americans") began in [Bainbridge Island, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bainbridge_Island,_Washington "Bainbridge Island, Washington").
*   **Born:**[Ruben Kun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruben_Kun "Ruben Kun"), [President of Nauru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Nauru "President of Nauru"), in [Nauru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nauru "Nauru") (d. 2014)

## [March 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_31 "March 31"), 1942 (Tuesday)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=March_1942&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: March 31, 1942 (Tuesday)")]

*   The Japanese began the [Indian Ocean raid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean_raid "Indian Ocean raid").
*   The [Battle of Christmas Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Christmas_Island "Battle of Christmas Island") was fought. Japanese soldiers were able to occupy [Christmas Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Island "Christmas Island") without resistance, although the American submarine _[Seawolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS\_Seawolf\_(SS-197) "USS Seawolf (SS-197)")_ damaged the Japanese cruiser _[Naka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_cruiser\_Naka "Japanese cruiser Naka")_.
*   Allied convoy [PQ 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_13 "Convoy PQ 13") reached [Murmansk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murmansk "Murmansk") despite fierce German attacks.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_1942#cite_note-chronicle_of_the_20th_c.-27)
*   German submarine _[U-353](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_submarine\_U-353 "German submarine U-353")_ was commissioned.

# World War II Wrecks: Graveyard of the Atlantic

 By [Caroline Glenn](https://www.scubadiving.com/taxonomy/term/1216) | Published On Januar 16, 2015

 Share This Article : [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic "(opens in a new window)")[](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic "(opens in a new window)")[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic "(opens in a new window)")[![Image 2: twitter](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8138585/255580473-e9e13421-89cf-445b-b2e2-e50e0864789f.svg)](https://twitter.com/share?text=Scubadiving:&url=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic&hashtags=scubadiving "(opens in a new window)")[](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/link/?url=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic "(opens in a new window)")

![Image 3](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/u701-film.jpg.webp?itok=HPTuuGiK)
> One of the most successful U-boats to patrol American waters during WWII, the U-701 had many accomplishments, among them, the sinking of the 14,000-ton _SS William Rockefeller_, according to the NOAA. On July 7, 1942, during a routine surfacing, the U-boat failed to spot a nearby U.S. Army aircraft. As she sank, she took seven sailors with her. Capt. Horst Degen and seven of his crewmembers survived and remained German prisoners of war until the end of the war. Discovered by scuba diver Uwe Lovas in 1989, 701 lies 10 miles off the coast from Avon, North Carolina. However, Lovas promised Degen he'd keep the vessel's location secret, and it was not rediscovered until 2004. Unfortunately, after the location was leaked to the diving public, the U-boat was heavily looted, but still remains in better shape than most other U-boats, according to the NOAA.
> 
> _Steve Sellers_

![Image 4](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/city-of-atlanta--10703.jpg.webp?itok=lpetSFB-)
> Sunk on Jan. 19, 1942, this 378-foot steam merchant vessel lies under almost 100 feet of water, just 18 miles north of Diamond Shoals, according to the NOAA. Built in 1904, the vessel met its fate soon after the tanker _Norness_ was torpedoed by the U-123 — the first casualty of the WWII U-boat attacks. Following the incident, the Navy ordered _City of Atlanta_ to hug the shore and dim its navigation lights. Despite its efforts, the vessel was torpedoed on the port side, shattering the pilothouse windows, according to Sunken Ships Outerbanks. A nearby freighter, the _Seatrain Texas,_ pulled five survivors of the 47-man crew out of the water six hours later.
> 
> _NOAA_

![Image 5](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/em-clark--11408.jpg.webp?itok=yhuuz-Ny)
> Sunk on March 18, 1942, this nearly 500-foot tanker now lies 20 miles south of Diamond Shoals in 72 feet of water, according to the NOAA. Built in 1921, E.M. Clark was struck by two torpedoes from U-124, sending it to the bottom of the ocean in just 10 minutes. With only one fatality, the 40 survivors were picked up by the Venezuelan steam tanker Catatumbo and the USS Dickerson, according to [uboat.net](http://www. uboat.net).
> 
> _NOAA_

![Image 6](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/hoyt-dixie-arrow_hr.jpg.webp?itok=yeNk3aMb)
> Sunk on March 26, 1942, this 485-foot tanker now lies 23 miles southwest of Diamond Shoals in about 90 feet of water, according to the NOAA. _Dixie Arrow_ and _Keshena \_rest within 5 miles of each other on the middle shelf in Raleigh Bay. Built in 1921, \_Dixie Arrow_ was part of a series of “Arrow”-named ships owned by what’s now known as Mobil gas, all of which were sunk during WWII.
> 
> 
> Traveling along Cape Hatteras to Paulsboro, New Jersey, the tanker was spotted by U-71 just as Capt. KK Walter Flascheenberg was about to order his U-boat to the bottom. Instead, he maneuvered between the _Dixie Arrow_ and the shore, and fired three torpedoes, sending the tanker up in flames and cracking it in two, according to NC Wreck Diving.
> 
> 
> As crewmembers tried to escape, wind-driven flames trapped a group of men. One seaman, Oscar G. Chappell, bravely repositioned the ship to free the men, which in turn directed the flames on himself. He was later posthumously awarded the Merchant Marine Distinguished Service Medal. The _SS\_\_ Oscar G. Chappell_ was also named in his honor, and today_,_ the Navy League annually awards the Able Seaman Oscar Chappell Award for Outstanding Maritime Stewardship.
> 
> 
> The flames were spotted by the _USS Tarbell,_ which picked up 22 survivors. In all, 11 crewmembers were killed. The U-71 escaped as one of the few U-boats to survive until the end of the war. The NC Marine Air Station used the remaining masts and wreck site for target practice until 1944, when it was wire-dragged and demolished at about 43 feet.
> 
> _NOAA_

![Image 7](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/u-352_casserley_0136.jpg.webp?itok=8KOOf5zi)
> Sunk on May 9, 1942, this German U-boat represents a significant piece of history as the fourth U-boat to be sunk by the United States during World War II, according to the NOAA. The 33 survivors were also the first German prisoners of war taken by the U.S. after declaration of war. Lying in more than 100 feet of water, the wreck site also holds the remains of 15 German soldiers who were killed in action at the hands of the U.S. Coast Guard patrol vessel _Icarus_, captained by Kapitanleutnant Rathke, according to the U.S. Coast Guard.
> 
> _NOAA_

World War II wrecks have been the sharp focus of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration for many years now, namely those buried in the Graveyard of the Atlantic. A patch of North Carolina waters, the iconic location is the resting place of a handful of American vessels and German U-boats that sunk during the Battle of the Atlantic.

# World War II Wrecks: Graveyard of the Atlantic

 By [Caroline Glenn](https://www.scubadiving.com/taxonomy/term/1216) | Published On Januar 16, 2015

 Share This Article : [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic "(opens in a new window)")[](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic "(opens in a new window)")[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic "(opens in a new window)")[![Image 2: twitter](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8138585/255580473-e9e13421-89cf-445b-b2e2-e50e0864789f.svg)](https://twitter.com/share?text=Scubadiving:&url=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic&hashtags=scubadiving "(opens in a new window)")[](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/link/?url=https://www.scubadiving.com/de/world-war-ii-wrecks-graveyard-atlantic "(opens in a new window)")

![Image 3](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/u701-film.jpg.webp?itok=HPTuuGiK)
> One of the most successful U-boats to patrol American waters during WWII, the U-701 had many accomplishments, among them, the sinking of the 14,000-ton _SS William Rockefeller_, according to the NOAA. On July 7, 1942, during a routine surfacing, the U-boat failed to spot a nearby U.S. Army aircraft. As she sank, she took seven sailors with her. Capt. Horst Degen and seven of his crewmembers survived and remained German prisoners of war until the end of the war. Discovered by scuba diver Uwe Lovas in 1989, 701 lies 10 miles off the coast from Avon, North Carolina. However, Lovas promised Degen he'd keep the vessel's location secret, and it was not rediscovered until 2004. Unfortunately, after the location was leaked to the diving public, the U-boat was heavily looted, but still remains in better shape than most other U-boats, according to the NOAA.
> 
> _Steve Sellers_

![Image 4](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/city-of-atlanta--10703.jpg.webp?itok=lpetSFB-)
> Sunk on Jan. 19, 1942, this 378-foot steam merchant vessel lies under almost 100 feet of water, just 18 miles north of Diamond Shoals, according to the NOAA. Built in 1904, the vessel met its fate soon after the tanker _Norness_ was torpedoed by the U-123 — the first casualty of the WWII U-boat attacks. Following the incident, the Navy ordered _City of Atlanta_ to hug the shore and dim its navigation lights. Despite its efforts, the vessel was torpedoed on the port side, shattering the pilothouse windows, according to Sunken Ships Outerbanks. A nearby freighter, the _Seatrain Texas,_ pulled five survivors of the 47-man crew out of the water six hours later.
> 
> _NOAA_

![Image 5](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/em-clark--11408.jpg.webp?itok=yhuuz-Ny)
> Sunk on March 18, 1942, this nearly 500-foot tanker now lies 20 miles south of Diamond Shoals in 72 feet of water, according to the NOAA. Built in 1921, E.M. Clark was struck by two torpedoes from U-124, sending it to the bottom of the ocean in just 10 minutes. With only one fatality, the 40 survivors were picked up by the Venezuelan steam tanker Catatumbo and the USS Dickerson, according to [uboat.net](http://www. uboat.net).
> 
> _NOAA_

![Image 6](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/hoyt-dixie-arrow_hr.jpg.webp?itok=yeNk3aMb)
> Sunk on March 26, 1942, this 485-foot tanker now lies 23 miles southwest of Diamond Shoals in about 90 feet of water, according to the NOAA. _Dixie Arrow_ and _Keshena \_rest within 5 miles of each other on the middle shelf in Raleigh Bay. Built in 1921, \_Dixie Arrow_ was part of a series of “Arrow”-named ships owned by what’s now known as Mobil gas, all of which were sunk during WWII.
> 
> 
> Traveling along Cape Hatteras to Paulsboro, New Jersey, the tanker was spotted by U-71 just as Capt. KK Walter Flascheenberg was about to order his U-boat to the bottom. Instead, he maneuvered between the _Dixie Arrow_ and the shore, and fired three torpedoes, sending the tanker up in flames and cracking it in two, according to NC Wreck Diving.
> 
> 
> As crewmembers tried to escape, wind-driven flames trapped a group of men. One seaman, Oscar G. Chappell, bravely repositioned the ship to free the men, which in turn directed the flames on himself. He was later posthumously awarded the Merchant Marine Distinguished Service Medal. The _SS\_\_ Oscar G. Chappell_ was also named in his honor, and today_,_ the Navy League annually awards the Able Seaman Oscar Chappell Award for Outstanding Maritime Stewardship.
> 
> 
> The flames were spotted by the _USS Tarbell,_ which picked up 22 survivors. In all, 11 crewmembers were killed. The U-71 escaped as one of the few U-boats to survive until the end of the war. The NC Marine Air Station used the remaining masts and wreck site for target practice until 1944, when it was wire-dragged and demolished at about 43 feet.
> 
> _NOAA_

![Image 7](https://www.scubadiving.com/sites/default/files/styles/655_1x_webp/public/trevor/u-352_casserley_0136.jpg.webp?itok=8KOOf5zi)
> Sunk on May 9, 1942, this German U-boat represents a significant piece of history as the fourth U-boat to be sunk by the United States during World War II, according to the NOAA. The 33 survivors were also the first German prisoners of war taken by the U.S. after declaration of war. Lying in more than 100 feet of water, the wreck site also holds the remains of 15 German soldiers who were killed in action at the hands of the U.S. Coast Guard patrol vessel _Icarus_, captained by Kapitanleutnant Rathke, according to the U.S. Coast Guard.
> 
> _NOAA_

World War II wrecks have been the sharp focus of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration for many years now, namely those buried in the Graveyard of the Atlantic. A patch of North Carolina waters, the iconic location is the resting place of a handful of American vessels and German U-boats that sunk during the Battle of the Atlantic.

**Quinine** is an [alkaloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkaloid "Alkaloid") used medically to treat [malaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaria "Malaria") and [babesiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babesiosis "Babesiosis").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4) This includes the treatment of malaria due to _[Plasmodium falciparum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmodium\_falciparum "Plasmodium falciparum")_ that is resistant to [chloroquine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroquine "Chloroquine") when [artesunate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artesunate "Artesunate") is not available.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-5) While sometimes used for [nocturnal leg cramps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nocturnal_leg_cramps "Nocturnal leg cramps"), quinine is not recommended for this purpose due to the risk of serious [side effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side_effect "Side effect").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4) It can be taken by mouth or [intravenously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intravenously "Intravenously").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4) Malaria resistance to quinine occurs in certain areas of the world.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-:0-6) Quinine is also used as an ingredient in [tonic water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonic_water "Tonic water") and other beverages to impart a bitter taste.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-olmsted-7)

Common side effects include headache, [ringing in the ears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tinnitus "Tinnitus"), vision issues, and [sweating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweating "Sweating").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4) More severe side effects include [deafness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deafness "Deafness"), [low blood platelets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrombocytopenia "Thrombocytopenia"), and an [irregular heartbeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irregular_heartbeat "Irregular heartbeat").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4) Use can make one more prone to [sunburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunburn "Sunburn").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4) While it is unclear if use during pregnancy carries potential for fetal harm, treating malaria during pregnancy with quinine when appropriate is still recommended.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4) Quinine possesses a C 9 H 7 N[quinoline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinoline "Quinoline")[functional group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_group "Functional group") ([pyridine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyridine "Pyridine") fused to [benzene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzene "Benzene")).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4)

Quinine was first isolated in 1820 from the bark of a [cinchona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinchona "Cinchona") tree, which is native to [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-AHFS2020-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-9) and its molecular formula was determined by [Adolph Strecker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolph_Strecker "Adolph Strecker") in 1854.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-10) The class of chemical compounds to which it belongs is thus called the cinchona alkaloids. Bark extracts had been used to treat malaria since at least 1632 and it was introduced to Spain as early as 1636 by [Jesuit missionaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesuit_missionaries "Jesuit missionaries") returning from the [New World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_World "New World").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-11) It is on the [World Health Organization's List of Essential Medicines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHO_Model_List_of_Essential_Medicines "WHO Model List of Essential Medicines").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-WHO23rd-12) Treatment of malaria with quinine marks the first known use of a chemical compound to treat an infectious disease.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-13)

## Uses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Quinine&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Uses")]

### Medical

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Quinine&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Medical")]

As of 2006, quinine is no longer recommended by the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") (WHO) as a first-line treatment for [malaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaria "Malaria"), because there are other substances that are equally effective with fewer side effects. They recommend that it be used only when [artemisinins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artemisinin#Artemisinin_derivatives "Artemisinin") are not available.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-17) Quinine is also used to treat [lupus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systemic_lupus_erythematosus "Systemic lupus erythematosus") and [arthritis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthritis "Arthritis").

Quinine was frequently prescribed as an [off-label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-label "Off-label") treatment for [leg cramps at night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cramps#Nocturnal_leg_cramps "Cramps"), but this has become less common since 2010 due to a warning from the US [Food and Drug Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_and_Drug_Administration "Food and Drug Administration") (FDA) that such practice is associated with life-threatening side effects.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-FDA_Safety_Communication-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-FDA_risks-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-20) Quinine can also act as a competitive inhibitor of [monoamine oxidase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monoamine_oxidase "Monoamine oxidase") (MAO), an enzyme that removes neurotransmitters from the brain. As an [MAO inhibitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monoamine_oxidase_inhibitor "Monoamine oxidase inhibitor"), it has potential to serve as a treatment for individuals with psychological disorders, similar to antidepressants that inhibit MAO.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-21)

#### Available forms

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Quinine&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Available forms")]

Quinine is a basic [amine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amine "Amine") and is usually provided as a salt. Various existing preparations include the [hydrochloride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrochloride "Hydrochloride"), dihydrochloride, [sulfate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulfate "Sulfate"), bisulfate and [gluconate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gluconate "Gluconate"). In the United States, quinine sulfate is commercially available in 324 mg tablets under the brand name Qualaquin.

All quinine salts may be given orally or [intravenously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intravenous_therapy "Intravenous therapy") (IV); quinine gluconate may also be given [intramuscularly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intramuscular_injection "Intramuscular injection") (IM) or rectally (PR).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-Barennes1996-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-Barennes2006-23) The main problem with rectal administration is that the dose can be expelled before it is completely absorbed; in practice, this is corrected by giving a further half dose. No injectable preparation of quinine is licensed in the US; [quinidine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinidine "Quinidine") is used instead.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinine_sulfate#cite_note-25)
